name: ε Indi B
what_it_is: a pair of brown dwarfs (types T1 and T6, called Ba and Bb) that orbit the star epsilon Indi A

motion.how_measured: position measured in each WISE image, then a straight-line fit through time

notes: 20 images were left out because a catalogue star was closer than 9" to the moving target (one SPHEREx pixel is 6.15"; such blends cannot be separated).
Peaks at 1.1–1.3, 1.6 and 2.1 µm (water absorption in between), a deep methane band at 3.2–3.5 µm (11.06 ± 0.13 mJy) and the brightest window at 3.9–4.2 µm (58.81 ± 0.55 mJy).
The methane band is at 19 % of the 4 µm peak and the flux drops again at 4.4–4.9 µm (19.20 ± 0.18 mJy; carbon monoxide): the classic shape of a T dwarf.
Ba and Bb (0.7" apart) are blended in SPHEREx's 6" pixels: this is their combined spectrum.
A 1100 K blackbody (dashed) does not fit: molecules (water, methane, CO) carve deep bands into the spectrum.

what_to_look_for_in_the_movie: a dot moving down and to the left (south-east) by about 66 arcseconds between 2010 and 2024
